results.title: What Are n8n Integrations and How Do They Work for You?
results.content:
Authentication is handled through credentials, which store the keys or tokens that let n8n access an app on your behalf. You set these up once, securely, and every workflow can use them. Data flows through the workflow as structured items, so the output of one integration, say a list of contacts from your CRM, becomes the input the next node acts on. Between nodes, you map and transform that data so each app receives it in the shape it expects. Most integration work is exactly this: connecting accounts, then mapping data correctly from one system to the next. When it is done carefully, the workflow is reliable; when it is rushed, it breaks the first time the data looks slightly different from expected.

## How to Set Up a New n8n Integration [...] Data mapping: Matching the fields and formats one system expects with what another provides is fiddly and a common source of silent errors. Test with real data, including the messy edge cases a quick test usually misses.

 Unavailable apps and unexpected data: Services go down and responses don’t always look the way you expect. Build in error handling so the workflow can recover or alert someone instead of failing quietly.

 Breaking changes: When an app updates its API, an integration built for the old version can stop working without warning. Monitor your workflows and maintain them over time so problems are caught early.

 Missing or immature nodes: A community node may not cover everything you need. In that case, the HTTP Request node or a custom build can fill the gap. [...] ## How to Set Up a New n8n Integration

Connecting a new app in n8n follows the same simple pattern regardless of the tool. First, you add the app’s node to your workflow, or the HTTP Request node if there is no dedicated one. Second, you create a credential: n8n walks you through connecting your account, usually by pasting an API key or signing in through the app, and stores it securely for reuse. Third, you configure the node to do what you want, choosing the action or trigger and mapping the data it should send or receive. Finally, you test it with real data before switching the workflow on.
